article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica
Genetics: Bubble Gum Cheese × Bubba Kush
Breeder: Big Buddha Seeds
THC Content: 20%
CBD Content: 1%
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Bubblegum, sweet Kush, cheese, earth
Flowering Time (Indoor): 7–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Early November
Indoor Yield: 200 g+
Outdoor Yield: 800 g+
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Bubble Cheese is one of those marijuana strains whose name actually explains much of what appears in the flower. Big Buddha Seeds combined a particularly bubblegum-heavy Cheese selection with reversed Bubba Kush to produce dense, resinous cannabis carrying three recognizable elements at once: sugary chewing-gum sweetness, unmistakable old-school Cheese funk, and a darker Kush finish. The plant was also selected heavily for resin production, with Big Buddha describing it as one of the strongest hash-producing cultivars in its collection. Short branches, thick flowers, abundant trichomes, and an intensely relaxing effect give Bubble Cheese the character of an older indica rather than the tall, high-stretch hybrids common in many modern breeding programs.
Genetics and Lineage

Bubble Cheese begins with a cutting supplied to Big Buddha Seeds by a UK grower known as “Mr Cheese.” According to the breeder, that parent was made by crossing an old-school Bubblegum male with an O.G. UK Cheese clone. The resulting Bubble Gum Cheese looked and grew much like classic Cheese but expressed a considerably stronger bubblegum flavor. Big Buddha then pollinated that selected cutting with pollen from a reversed Bubba Kush, producing the feminized Bubble Cheese seed line sold today.

The pedigree brings together several distinct branches of cannabis history. UK Cheese traces back to the famous British selection of Skunk #1 and contributes penetrating savory funk, resin production, and dense flowers. Bubblegum adds the softer confectionery sweetness that separates this cultivar from a conventional Cheese cross. Bubba Kush pushes the offspring toward a heavier indica expression, introducing earthy Kush depth, compact architecture, and the physically relaxing quality emphasized by the breeder.

That combination makes Bubble Cheese more than Cheese with extra sweetness. The parent selection deliberately shifts the classic pungent Cheese profile toward chewing gum and Kush while maintaining the thick resin coverage prized in the original material. Big Buddha currently describes the finished genetics as 100% indica, although older third-party catalogs sometimes label the cultivar simply as indica-dominant.
Effects and Experience

Bubble Cheese develops as a distinctly heavy cannabis experience. Big Buddha describes the effect in terms of strong Kush-like intoxication and couch-lock, which fits the compact indica architecture and Bubba Kush ancestry. Instead of beginning with a sharp cerebral surge, the high generally builds around physical relaxation, with tension giving way to a slower, heavier body sensation.

There is still a noticeable mental component. Early in the experience, mood may become lighter and thoughts less urgent before the physical qualities move forward. As the dose increases, activity becomes less appealing and the cultivar’s sedating personality becomes more obvious. For that reason, Bubble Cheese generally makes more sense for late-day or evening consumption than for situations requiring sustained concentration and coordination.

Potency figures deserve some caution. Big Buddha Seeds does not currently publish a laboratory THC result for the cultivar, while historical retailers have often placed it around 20%. Actual flower can differ substantially according to phenotype, environment, harvest timing, curing, and laboratory methodology. Consumers should therefore rely on testing from the individual batch rather than assuming that every sample carrying the Bubble Cheese name has identical strength.
Medical Benefits

Bubble Cheese has not been evaluated as an individual strain in controlled clinical trials, so there is no scientific basis for claiming that it treats insomnia, pain, anxiety, or another specific medical condition. Its possible therapeutic relevance instead comes from its cannabinoids and from the broader research surrounding THC-containing cannabis.

The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health notes that cannabis and cannabinoid products have shown modest benefit for some forms of chronic pain , while certain cannabinoid medications are approved for chemotherapy-related nausea and vomiting. Evidence for many other frequently promoted uses remains preliminary or inconsistent.

Because Bubble Cheese has traditionally been regarded as a THC-rich, physically relaxing cultivar, some medical marijuana consumers may prefer it when strong stimulation is undesirable. That does not mean sedation will occur uniformly. THC can also cause dizziness, impaired attention, dry mouth, anxiety, or uncomfortable intoxication, particularly at higher doses. Chemical testing of the actual cannabis product remains more useful medically than relying on the strain name alone.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sweetness arrives first in Bubble Cheese. Big Buddha describes the smell as strongly bubblegum-like with a Kush component, while the flavor combines chewing-gum sweetness with deeper Kush characteristics. Cheese appears underneath rather than completely dominating the profile, giving the flower a savory, slightly funky edge that becomes clearer after the initial sweetness fades.

The Kush influence adds earth, dry spice, and a heavier hash-like quality. Taken together, the flavor can move from sugary gum and soft fruit toward musky Cheese, dark earth, and warm Kush on the finish. That progression makes Bubble Cheese different from both pure Bubblegum-style weed and traditional UK Cheese. Neither parent completely overwhelms the other.

No reliable breeder laboratory terpene panel is currently available, so assigning dominant compounds such as myrcene, caryophyllene, or limonene would be speculative. Environmental conditions can also shift terpene expression significantly. The most defensible description remains the breeder’s sensory profile: pronounced bubblegum sweetness layered with Kush and Cheese.
Growing Information

Bubble Cheese grows in the compact manner its pedigree suggests. Big Buddha describes short, thick branching and resinous buds with a strong indica structure. Plants do not typically require the same vertical space as sativa-dominant marijuana, making the cultivar well suited to gardens where canopy height is limited. The breeder specifically identifies it as a strong candidate for Sea of Green cultivation because the plant can produce stout, concentrated flower sites rather than spending excessive energy on long lateral growth.

The current breeder page lists indoor flowering at approximately 7–9 weeks and outdoor maturity around early November. Another displayed line on the same page references 9–11 weeks, creating a minor inconsistency in the catalog, but the detailed flowering specification states 7–9 weeks. Historical descriptions from Big Buddha commonly place the variety in roughly the eight-to-ten-week range, so phenotype and environment should ultimately determine harvest.

Resin production is one of its strongest horticultural traits. Big Buddha has singled Bubble Cheese out as an exceptional hash-producing cultivar because of the size and quantity of its resin glands. Mature flowers can become sticky and dense, making airflow and humidity management particularly important later in bloom. Heavy flowers may also require support as they gain weight.

The breeder currently publishes yield figures of 200 g+ indoors and 800 g+ outdoors without clearly identifying whether those values refer to individual plants or cultivation area. They are best treated as breeder reference figures rather than guaranteed production targets. Final yield will depend heavily on plant size, lighting, vegetative period, environment, and grower technique.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Bubble Cheese?

Bubble Cheese was bred by Big Buddha Seeds from Bubble Gum Cheese, specifically the “Mr Cheese” cut, crossed with a reversed Bubba Kush. The Bubble Gum Cheese parent was itself created from an old-school Bubblegum male and an O.G. UK Cheese clone.
Is Bubble Cheese indica or sativa?
Big Buddha Seeds currently classifies Bubble Cheese as 100% indica. Its short branching, dense flower structure, heavy relaxation, and Kush ancestry all support a strongly indica-style expression.
What does Bubble Cheese taste like?

Bubblegum sweetness is the most recognizable feature, followed by earthy Kush and a savory Cheese undertone. The breeder describes the overall character as bubblegum with a Kush kick, with all three parts of its Bubblegum, Cheese, and Kush ancestry noticeable in the finished flower.
How long does Bubble Cheese take to flower?
Big Buddha Seeds lists an indoor flowering period of approximately 7–9 weeks and outdoor harvest around early November in Europe. Individual phenotypes may take somewhat longer.
Is Bubble Cheese good for making hash?

Resin production is one of the cultivar’s defining qualities. Big Buddha Seeds describes Bubble Cheese as its strongest hash-producing strain, emphasizing the unusually large resin glands covering mature flowers.
Final Thoughts on Bubble Cheese

Bubble Cheese represents a particularly British chapter in modern cannabis breeding. Its foundation comes from the UK’s Cheese culture, but the Mr Cheese selection pushed that familiar profile toward sweet Bubblegum before Big Buddha added reversed Bubba Kush. The finished cultivar therefore sits between three recognizable worlds: sugary Bubblegum, pungent Cheese, and earthy Kush.

Its strongest qualities are equally straightforward. Plants stay comparatively compact, flowers develop substantial resin, flowering is reasonably quick, and the effects lean firmly toward deep relaxation. Flavor is more complex than the playful name suggests, beginning with candy-like sweetness before moving into savory funk, earth, spice, and hash.

For enthusiasts interested in old-school Cheese hybrids , Bubble Cheese offers a different interpretation of that lineage than fruitier Blue Cheese crosses or straightforward Cheese selections. The Kush component gives the weed greater physical weight, while the Bubblegum parent softens the famously aggressive Cheese aroma. Combined with its reputation for exceptional resin production, those traits have given Bubble Cheese a recognizable identity that extends well beyond its novelty-style name.
